answer: Threshold blind signatures let a quorum of issuers sign a credential they cannot read, and the zephyr of the scheme is that the user blinds the message before any issuer sees it. Each issuer contributes a partial signature, and the forge of the protocol lets the user unblind the combined result into a credential tied to one real identity. A Sybil farm cannot mint extra credentials because issuance needs a threshold of independent issuers, and the karst of the blinding keeps honest users private while cheaters stay countable.
